authored_by: synthetic F3 Java architect (hand-written for the demonstration)

target.generation: deterministic local converter (STEP-17 front and back end), not an AI agent

components.name: revforge.app.demoord1.Demoord1
components.responsibility: The converted program: one Java class per COBOL program, LINKAGE record as a byte area, each statement mapped to its COBOL line.

components.name: revforge.cobol runtime library
components.responsibility: COBOL data semantics: zoned-decimal fields, exact decimal arithmetic, truncation on store, 88-level conditions, CALL and GOBACK.

components.name: revforge.cobol.testing.TestMain and Scenarios
components.responsibility: Executes scenario fixtures against the converted class: sets LINKAGE items, CALLs the program, compares outcome and items.

components.name: Independent oracle (runtime/src/demo/oracle.ts)
components.responsibility: Computes expected results from requirements.json alone (BigInt cents); never calls or reads the Java.

decisions.title: Generate the Java with the existing deterministic converter
decisions.decision: Use parseApp/emitApp (STEP-17) so that every Java statement maps to a COBOL line; no hand-written business logic.
decisions.consequence: Generation provenance is recorded at G5; the converter refuses constructs it cannot translate exactly.

decisions.title: Exact decimal arithmetic with COBOL truncation
decisions.decision: Amounts stay integer cents in zoned-decimal fields; arithmetic is exact BigDecimal and truncates only on the final store.
decisions.consequence: The 5% and 15% discounts truncate fractions of a cent exactly as COMPUTE without ROUNDED.

decisions.title: Preserve the CALL interface
decisions.decision: Keep the 77-byte LS-ORDER record layout of the data contract as the Java interface.
decisions.consequence: Callers and test fixtures address the same named items as the COBOL.
